title: Applying the Grating Equation
text: For n=1: d sin(theta) = lambda, so sin(theta) = lambda/d = (550 x 10^-9)/(2 x 10^-6) = 550/2000 = 0.275

title: Finding the Angle
text: theta = arcsin(0.275) = 15.96 degrees. Diffraction gratings separate light into its component wavelengths, which is why they are used in spectrometers to analyse the composition of light sources like stars.
